proof.text: The exponent-one coefficient ideal is the principal ideal of the recorded uniformizer. The uniformizer property from [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] identifies it with the recorded maximal ideal, so the quotient is a field. Fix a slice U and an arbitrary module sheaf L over its restricted constant residue ring. The restricted constant-ring unit in [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf] is locally surjective. For each finite relation in L, intersect the image covering sieves of its coefficients. On each resulting arrow the coefficients lift to residue-field elements. Restrict the scalar action on the section module along the field-to-sections map; this is a vector space, hence flat. Mathlib Module.Flat.isTrivialRelation_of_sum_smul_eq_zero gives a finite factorization of the lifted relation. Map its matrix coefficients back to the ring sheaf. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-equational-criterion-universes] to conclude L is flat in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Empty covering sieves and zero-length relations are included.

proof.text: Restrict the canonical representative of K_1 termwise to the slice. By exactness of restriction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], the homology of this complex is the restriction of the original homology. DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors and the representative isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] therefore give zero homology in every degree outside [a,b]. This is the actual ringedSiteDerivedRestrictionOfUniverses, with all universes explicit, not evaluation on an object.

proof.text: Resolve the canonical representative of K_1 restricted to U by the same selected K-flat resolution P used in the definition of ringedSiteDerivedTensorOfUniverses [lem-pc-kflat-resolution, def-pc-kflat-complex]. Show tensoring by P preserves quasi-isomorphisms in the second variable. A quasi-isomorphism has acyclic cone [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]; K-flatness kills tensoring the cone on the other side, and the signed flip of total complexes and the sectionwise braiding interchange the sides. The tensor/cone comparison [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] then proves the required quasi-isomorphism. Additivity of tensor and its explicit-to-monoidal comparison come from [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits].

proof.text: Localize the quasi-isomorphism-inverting functor P tensor - followed by Q. Its factorization isomorphism lets us replace the canonical representative of L[0] by the actual single complex L[0]. The single-complex total tensor comparison identifies the result with termwise tensorRight L applied to P. Step 1 and the explicit-to-monoidal comparison [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] make tensorRight L exact. The short-complex mapHomologyIso identifies its degree-i homology with tensorRight L applied to H^i(P). The resolution quasi-isomorphism identifies the latter homology with that of the restricted K_1, zero by step 2. Exact tensor preserves zero, proving the conclusion for every U,L,i. No local-model finiteness, affineness, weak contractibility, completeness, or truncation filtration is needed.

title: Flat bounded cohomology gives finite Tor amplitude
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and its residue field $k=R/(\varpi)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $V$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] weakly contractible for its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], meaning that evaluation on $V$ sends every epimorphism of sheaves of sets to a surjection. Put $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(R/\varpi^n)_V$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be derived complete for its coefficient quotient tower [def-weil-derived-complete]. Write $k_V$ for the constant sheaf of residue fields [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and $K_1=K\otimes^L_B k_V$, the derived reduction modulo $\varpi$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] (here $k_V=(R/\varpi)_V$). Suppose $a\leq b$ are integers, $H^q(K_1)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and each $H^q(K_1)$ is locally constant with finite-dimensional $k$-vector-space local models [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. Then for every object $U\to V$ of $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$, every sheaf $L$ of $k_U$-modules, and every $i\notin[a,b]$, one has
$$H^i\bigl((K_1|_U)\otimes^L_{k_U}L\bigr)=0,$$
where $k_U=k_V|_U$ and restriction is to the localized site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-derived-restriction]. Thus the residue complex has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ on every slice, not just after evaluation on $V$.
